citation.description: reconcile.py docstring explicitly documents the root cause (bug 9f63): cursor advanced unconditionally to newest, abandoning candidates. Lines 20-28 describe the mechanism and fix.

criteria.criterion: Root cause established for why the upload event does not queue a review — proven, not inferred. Runtime experiment (3 reconcile passes, `since`-honouring events-log double) plus a live events-log probe proving `?t1=` is a server-side inclusive lower bound; see the RCA comment.

citation.description: Test exists, runs two passes, asserts abandoned candidate (Istale) is re-driven on pass 2 (line 1989) and cursor does not advance past its event time (line 1997).

criteria.criterion: A patch-set upload that the webhook drops is re-driven WITHOUT any manual comment. `tests/unit/test_review_bot.py::test_reconcile_cursor_holds_back_an_abandoned_non_newest_candidate` — two passes, a multi-event window, the abandoned NON-newest candidate re-driven on pass 2.

citation.description: Test exists, asserts cursor advances to newest event time (3000) when a change returns skipped/post_vote_closed.

criteria.criterion: A terminal outcome does NOT pin the cursor. `test_reconcile_cursor_advances_past_a_terminal_outcome` — a `skipped`/`post_vote_closed` candidate lets the cursor advance to the newest event.

criteria.criterion: A chronically-failing candidate cannot pin the window forever. `test_reconcile_holdback_is_bounded_so_a_poison_pill_cannot_pin_the_window` — past `RECONCILE_MAX_HOLDBACK_SECONDS` the cursor advances and `RECONCILE_DEGRADED reason=holdback_expired` is emitted.
